clue.text: Entertained by commercial featuring Clio, perhaps

indicators.note: an advert featuring something carries it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
Clio is the Greek Muse of history; 'perhaps' marks her as an example

explanation.surface: Someone was charmed by a TV advert starring a Clio, the Renault car.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio reads as the Renault hatchback from TV adverts, but here she is the Greek Muse of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to have been diverted or kept happily occupied, a straightforward synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Forge perfect bundle

blocks.note: first meaning: to make coins by stamping metal
second meaning: as new, in pristine condition
third meaning: a large sum of money, as in 'it cost a packet'

explanation.surface: Instructions to hammer out a flawless package at a smithy.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: three separate senses of one four-letter word strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to stamp coins, describes something in pristine new condition, and is informal for a huge amount of money.

clue.text: Choice of the Spanish in part

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, so the short Spanish word goes within the longer one

blocks.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a section is a part

explanation.surface: Someone is picking, partly, from Spanish options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' reads as 'partly', but 'in' is the container signal and 'part' supplies the outer word: SE(EL)CTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a choice, both meaning the thing or things picked out from a range.

clue.text: Hang Duke by corner

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: A sinister order to execute a nobleman in a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang loosely or swing from something, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Unhappiness of sadists upset about international group

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the abbreviation for international
a faction is a group within a larger body

explanation.surface: Some cruel people are cross about an international organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first word is jumbled; the abbreviation sits near its end, and the group word is simply added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissatisfaction is discontent or displeasure, a feeling of not being content, so it matches unhappiness.

clue.text: Watch voyeurs playing without ball

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about in a game, giving a new order
without means lacking, so the round letter is removed first

blocks.note: taken as written
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Peeping Toms at a match watch the players while the ball is out of play.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from VOYEURS to leave VYEURS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey is to look over or observe carefully, so it works as a verb synonym for watch.

clue.text: Sat following drink and considered

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for sat is placed after the word for drink

blocks.note: to sup is to drink, or a sup is a mouthful
to pose is to sit for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone sat down after a drink and thought things over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sat is meant in the artist's-model sense: a sitter poses for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means assumed or believed, so something supposed has been considered or thought to be so.

clue.text: Spanish wine and Brazilian port getting positive response from Germany

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine and a Brazilian fortified drink win approval from German tasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink alongside wine; it is the city of Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Former journalists oddly disown word or phrase

indicators.note: oddly means in an odd fashion, taking every other letter of the following word

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the press is journalists collectively
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Ex-reporters strangely reject something somebody said.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'oddly' gives the even-placed letters of disown: alternate letters either way round.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression is a set phrase or particular form of words, an idiom or saying.

clue.text: Suspicions of Heather being covered in tattoos

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: inks is slang for tattoos
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: People suspect a woman called Heather of being heavily tattooed.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the moorland shrub, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Inklings are faint ideas or vague notions, close in meaning to suspicions or hunches.

clue.text: In favour of politician having time for cause

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
MP is Member of Parliament
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Supporting an MP who has time for a cause they champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' looks like a noun, a campaign, but the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt is to bring about or give rise to something, the verb sense of cause.

clue.text: Joined forces with strangely adorable clot

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the following letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone teamed up with a lovable idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: A clot is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate is to work together on a shared task, so the past tense means joined forces.

clue.text: Deliver detective inspector's commendation

blocks.note: DI is detective inspector, plus the 's
a tribute is an act of praise

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hand over a police officer's award.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is kept as a letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out or give out goods to people, as a delivery round does.

clue.text: Small matter involving national industry leaders

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so each word supplies its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A trivial issue that concerns the heads of nationalised industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small matter' looks like the definition phrase; only 'Small' defines, and 'matter' starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini is used as an adjective or prefix meaning miniature or tiny, as in a mini skirt.

clue.text: Dreamer I trade with first

blocks.note: taken as written
to deal is to trade
1st written with the numeral read as I

explanation.surface: A self-described dreamer says they would rather trade first.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written 1st, and the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty, often unrealistic principles, so is commonly called a dreamer or visionary.

clue.text: Obtain playground equipment to get overwhelming election victory

blocks.note: to land a job is to obtain it
a slide is a piece of playground equipment

explanation.surface: A politician buys new playground slides to win votes by a huge margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is a decisive win in which one party takes a vast majority of seats or votes.

clue.text: Post Office buries clues

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: The postal service hides away evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointers are hints or tips that steer someone toward an answer, just as clues do.

clue.text: Tolerate rotten deadlock

blocks.note: to stand something is to put up with it
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with a corrupt impasse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a stalemate in which neither side will give way, just like a deadlock.

clue.text: Negative about time of day

blocks.note: no is a negative reply
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy about what hour it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock, a specific point in the daily cycle.

clue.text: Touched middle of disc in overturned writing table

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the inner letters are kept
overturned in a down answer means turned upside down, so the furniture word runs bottom to top
in places the centre letters inside the furniture word

blocks.note: the two central letters
a desk is a writing table

explanation.surface: Someone handled the centre of a record lying in a tipped-over bureau.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first; the two middle letters then go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have kissed is to have touched with the lips, and in snooker or bowls balls that kiss lightly touch.

clue.text: Dish with notches on angle

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across answer, so the notches word follows the angle word

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
and means with or together with
chips are small nicks or notches

explanation.surface: A plate with nicks around a sloping rim.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word does double duty: 'Dish' looks like crockery, and 'angle' reads as geometry rather than fishing. Fish and chips is Britain's classic takeaway of battered fish with fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and chips is a single classic meal, a dish in the sense of a prepared course of food.

clue.text: Thing engineered to hold sort of joint

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the words before carry the answer inside them

blocks.note: found running across the two words, after the opening T

explanation.surface: A gadget is built to contain a type of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineered' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer is hidden in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is a pivoting joint, the kind on a door or lid, and the knee is called a hinge joint.

clue.text: Laze around, showing enthusiasm

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved round and about into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idler lounging about is somehow full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a contradiction: lazing yet keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal is great energy or fervour for a cause, a close synonym for eager enthusiasm.

clue.text: Tree is one of five on borders of college

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies at one birth
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A quintuplet studies at the edge of a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a small fruit tree of the rose family, grown for its hard pear-shaped fruit.

clue.text: Popular feature of church deacon originally encouraged

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower
its first letter

explanation.surface: A well-liked part of the church service was cheered on by the deacon.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to fill them with confidence or the urge to act, much as encouragement does.

clue.text: Small jugs forming waste disposal system

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the definition reads it as a network taken as a whole

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ewers are large water jugs

explanation.surface: A few little jugs are pressed into service as drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewers are the underground pipes and channels carrying away wastewater, together forming a drainage network.

clue.text: Lives comfortably in outskirts of Dungeness

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters of the place name are kept
in places the word for comfortably inside those edge letters

blocks.note: its first and last letters
living well means living comfortably

explanation.surface: Someone lives a cosy life on the edge of Dungeness, a shingle headland in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives comfortably' looks like one phrase; only 'Lives' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make one's home there, the verb sense of lives.
